scientific_question: Does baseline pollen limitation modify the incremental effect of imposed pollinator-activity decline on the evolution of assurance A versus investment I?
interpretation_exclusions: Cannot infer responsiveness from zero terminal contrast alone; both arms can hit a common allele bound
Baseline effectiveness manipulates pollen delivery rather than just number of visitors
No automatic claim that pollinator decline has no influence on A, nor that A responds to the derivative of historical change
Homogeneous exogenous visitor assembly is not a stochastic visitor-history experiment
No natural island effect, genetic mediation, population-wide evolutionary law or restored-environment adaptation

cohort.founder_allele_processing: native reflect_unit then nearest grid node, ties to lower node
cohort.pairing: match control and decline by founder and demographic stream, using same prefix and stochastic RNG streams; followup streams inherit the matched RNG state and diverge only after different birth outcomes

analysis.unit_of_independent_resampling: founder seed, not demographic replicate or paired arm
analysis.primary_descriptive_target: initial-A-stratified interaction on post-prefix changes in assurance: [(A80-A30)_decline - (A80-A30)_control]_weak_limit - same_strong_limit
secondary_targets: A30-A0 and I30-I0 by baseline pollen-limitation level
A and I final differences between decline and control at each baseline level
within-founder variance, endpoint diversity, non-events, allele maximum and minimum
first/last census q, realized selfed and outcrossed production, and occupancy
analysis.alternative_start_sensitivity: A0 0.3 compared with 0.5; never discard either starting state
analysis.survivor_rule: Report unconditional all-start occupancy; A and I are undefined after extinction, and trait contrasts have explicit survivor-conditioned denominators
analysis.uncertainty: founder cluster bootstrap interval descriptive only; no preregistered p-value or model-general claim
